question: AI valuations are at all-time highs. Should we pull our AI investment activity for 6 months?
baseline_answer:

The brain has no direct evidence on whether pausing AI investment for 6 months is the right call. It does hold a track record of garry's past macro-timing calls on AI, and those calls were wrong.

- Garry predicted "AI hype cycle peaks by Q3 2024" with conviction weight 0.85. The outcome was incorrect [cat14/cat14-pos-3-macro/take-1].
- Garry predicted "AI valuations correct by year-end 2024" with conviction weight 0.8. The outcome was incorrect [cat14/cat14-pos-3-macro/take-2].
- Garry predicted "The bubble pops in 2025" with conviction weight 0.85. The outcome was incorrect [cat14/cat14-pos-3-macro/take-3].

All three resolved takes are in the macro-timing domain, all were held at high conviction (0.8–0.85), and all were wrong. Each was a call that AI valuations or hype would turn down. A pause justified by high valuations would rest on a similar timing view. The brain's record shows that this kind of call has not worked for garry so far.

These three takes are a small sample. They show that past timing calls on valuation peaks were wrong. They do not show that valuations today are justified, or that a pause would be a mistake. The brain holds no takes on current (2026) valuations, on the fund's own AI portfolio performance, or on the cost of sitting out for 6 months.
